 P.A.TO JUDGE sts  SHAJI P.CHALY, J.
Dated this the 8th day of January 2018
JUDGMENT Petitioners are registered owners of goods vehicle bearing Nos.KL.46.M 6587 and KL.7.Q 919.

In the vehicles parked by the side of the road, goods prohibited for sale under the Food Safety and Standards Act (herein after referred to as `FSS Act' for short) was found out and the vehicles consequently were taken possession of by the foods safety authority and removed to the concerned Police Stations.
The grievances highlighted by the petitioners in these writ petitions are common in nature and therefore, I heard them together and propose to pass a common judgment.

2. The legal contention advanced is that even though the Foods Safety authority is entitled to take samples of the products found in the vehicle, they are not vested with the powers under the FSS Act or any other Rules to detain the vehicle.
It is thus seeking appropriate directions, this writ petition is filed.

3. When the matter came up for admission before this court, a learned Single judge found that there is every likelihood of tax element, in the products found out in the vehicles and therefore, the Shyghon vs The Food Safety Officer on 28 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189751928/

sentences.text: 3 concerned Commissioner of Commercial Tax is suo motu impleaded to this writ petition.
4. I have heard learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Special Government Pleader for Taxes and perused the pleadings and documents on record.
It is an admitted fact that there is no power vested with the authorities under the FSS Act or any other appended Rules, to detain any vehicles from where prohibited goods were found out.
Any how, the vehicles was entrusted by the food safety authority before the concerned Police Stations and the same is remaining there.
The stand of the Police is that if and when registered owner of the vehicle with appropriate documents approaches the Police, the vehicles can be released.

5. In that view of the matter, there will be a direction to the fifth respondent and second respondent respectively to release the vehicles in question, on the petitioners producing the proof and the identity of the vehicles and ownership of the vehicles, by securing a self bond from the petitioners for reasonable value.

I also make it clear that the issue with respect to the tax element, that is apprehended is left open and the appropriate statutory authority is at liberty to proceed against the consignment in accordance with law.
I also make it clear that I have not made any opinion with respect to the taxability of the goods found from the vehicles in question.
The writ petitions are disposed of accordingly.
Sd/ SHAJI P.CHALY JUDGE jm/
